focusDirective: waste frontier: cap-length runs, stalls beyond the fixed one, dead or inert paths; expected rung stated with shared-state reasoning

hypothesis.title: Learned stall cap: end a run once it has gone a learned number of steps without any handler writing state or any client or fault row
hypothesis.description: Add spur/spur-core/src/simulator/stall_cap.rs with the run_cap learner's shape verbatim (one histogram per configured step budget, checkpoints at 200/400/800 completed run-cap probes, cap = ceil(1.5 x the p99 cell's upper edge) clamped to the budget, identity below the floor, decay and reset beside run_cap's). The statistic it learns is a completed probe's longest quiet gap: the most steps the run ever went between two progress marks, counting the final segment up to plan completion. A progress mark is any of: (a) a non-timer history row (Invocation, Response, Crash, Recover, Partition, Heal); (b) a dispatched handler entry, delivery or timer firing, after which the node's state token differs from before (the same node_state_token compare the acted probes make at scheduler.rs:1450 and :1455, now taken at every entry regardless of emit_acted_fraction and returned on ScheduleResult::RecordExecuted and ::TimerFired as `acted: bool`); (c) a planned event released by the engine, a held client request issued, or a withheld crash landing. In exec_plan (path.rs) a per-run clock counts steps since the last mark and does not advance while a queued planned crash is withheld by a placement hold or a phase wait, while the client hold queue is non-empty, or while purgatory holds anything (each of those is a bounded, scheduler-owned future release). A run in the treated cell ends with a new RunOutcome::StallCapReached { cap, outstanding_events } (end_reason 'stall_cap_reached' in the runs table, RunEnd::StallCapReached folded into the termination and prefix_extension blocks) as soon as its clock exceeds the scope's stall cap. Treated cell: three of four salted phases of the run id under a salt of its own (share 0.75); run-cap probes and timer-context probes are exempt, so every learner feed (cap, placement, timer context, stall cap) sees exactly the runs it sees today. No config field. Tag STALL_CAP = 1 << 10 in run_variant.rs (bit 1024, the retired freshFirstDestCut row renamed stallCap in VARIANT_BITS). Counters: stall_cap.stops, stall_cap.treated_runs, stall_cap.untreated_runs, stall_cap.steps_saved_sum (effective cap minus stop step), stall_cap.suspended_steps_sum, stall_cap.marks.{rows,acted_deliveries,acted_timers,releases}, stall_cap.probes_keyed, stall_cap.probe_over_cap_completions (a completed probe whose longest gap exceeded the standing cap: the over-cap check run_cap already exports), stall_cap.scopes_learned and stall_cap.cap_max_scope gauges, termination.all.stall_cap_reached.
hypothesis.rationale: Baseline chunk (606,180 runs): learned_cap_reached 295,328 (49%), iterations_exhausted 194,220 (32%), plan_complete 116,301 (19%); steps_used_sum 1.38B of which cap-reached runs at 3,275 steps hold about 967M (70%); prefix_extension.steps_released_sum 1.355B of 1.380B and tail_without_release_sum 12,053, so the unfinished runs are not idle, they release runnables every step. A 60 s campaign session on the merged tree (69,632 runs, output in this session's scratchpad) shows what those runnables are: in cap-reached grid runs the last progress mark (client/fault row, or a log line that only a state-changing handler prints) sits at median step 444 of 3,131 and 73-75% of the run's steps come after it (tail p25 2,526, p50 2,669, p75 2,771); in grid-short's exhausted runs the last mark is at median 281 of 1,500 (tail share 60%). One such run (31765): node 0 crashed at step 205 and restarted at 206, its Recovery drew only backup responses so it never left recovering status, the planned Read at node 0 then looped on a self-redirect every 4-5 steps from 207 to 3,129, and the later restarts of nodes 1 and 2 stalled the same way; 65 of 3,131 steps were timer fires, the rest client-loop deliveries whose handlers write nothing. 18,100 of 19,086 cap-reached runs end with at least one node still in recovery (avg 1.89), 13,337 with node 0. The deadlock exit (331 per chunk) cannot fire because the client loop and the timer loop keep the queues non-empty. The learner feed is tight: completed run-cap probes' longest quiet gap reads p90 177, p99 410, p999 545, max 562 (n 662), so the 6000-scope cap lands near 615 steps; with a cap of 813, 84-87% of cap-reached grid runs have a tail longer than the cap and the cut removes 50-52% of their steps (40% at a cap of 1,200), and 22% of grid-short's exhausted steps. Tail steps are cheap (cap-reached runs average 5.8-6.3 us per step against 12-13.6 us for completing runs, so the tail costs about 4 us per step), which prices the wall saving at about 36% of a cap-reached run's wall and 25% of the session's wall on treated runs. The closed recover-settle-learned-stop keyed on the last fault-crossing delivery, whose tail is heavy (settles learned at 935-2,411 steps) and saved a sixth of treated steps for +6.5% per second; this key is the run's own state changes, whose completed-probe gap is a quarter of that, and a run that is progressing is never cut.
hypothesis.generalityArgument: The rule names no handler, message, role or timer label: a step is progress when it appends a client or fault row, when a dispatched handler wrote its node's state (the token compare every Spur role already carries), or when the plan released something. The cap is learned per session from that protocol's own completed probes with the constants run_cap already ships (quantile 0.99, headroom 1.5, floor 200), so a protocol whose runs legitimately go quiet for long stretches learns a long cap; the exported probe_over_cap_completions share says whether the cap cuts live runs (run_cap's twin reads 11 of 5,342 on the baseline). Every panel member's stuck states (a stale ballot that never wins, a candidate that never gets votes) are inert churn under the same definition.

prediction.mechanism: Treatment bit stallCap = 1 << 10, drawn by a salted phase of the run id (three phases of four treated, share 0.75 of non-probe runs; run-cap and timer-context probes exempt). The direct per-run effect is on length, not on events: a treated run keeps every step it would have taken up to the stall and loses only inert tail, so on the internal rung (depth>=8 per run, treated against co-bit-matched untreated) the honest prediction is preservation, [0.97, 1.03], while treated steps per run read [0.58, 0.78] on the long grid arms and [0.75, 0.95] on grid-short. The gain is delivered on the cross-binary rung: the whole candidate's depth>=8 events per explore-second against the baseline in [1.10, 1.28], carried by runs per second. Shared state: probes are exempt so the cap, placement and timer-context learners see the same samples; the arm-selector learners read rewards computed from events that all occur before a stall; a replay parent cut at its stall leaves a tape the child replays as a prefix either way, so the split by run id keeps tapes and plans consistent between parent and child. Judge note: the closed settle-stop cut a sixth of treated steps and read 1.065 against a predicted [1.10, 1.30]; this band's floor of 1.10 clears the 5% layout floor and the recorded 7-8% cross-session spread only at its low end, so a read in [1.05, 1.10) is unresolved, not confirmed. Both seeds of the fresh merged-tree cache (afeccdf6e8f7) are the paired baseline.
prediction.independentObservable: SEPARATION GATE, read on chunk 1 before any rung is credited (the read-only demonstration the closed stall-abort family demanded): export stall_cap.untreated_gap_over_cap.{depth6,depth8,depth10} and stall_cap.untreated_runs_at.{depth6,depth8,depth10} - on untreated non-probe runs (the stock quarter, which still ends at the learned cap) the longest quiet gap as this mechanism defines it, measured whether or not it exceeds the standing stall cap of the run's scope. The share of untreated depth>=8 runs whose longest gap exceeds the standing cap must be at or below 0.05, and at depth>=6 at or below 0.05; above 0.10 at either rung the cap is cutting the population that produces depth and the candidate closes on chunk 1 without a rung read. Also: stall_cap.probe_over_cap_completions at or below 2% of run_cap.probe_completions per chunk (the fresh merged baseline's run_cap twin reads 26/6010 = 0.43% on seed 1000 and 14/6179 = 0.23% on seed 1001); stall_cap.cap_max_scope between 450 and 900 steps for the 6000 budget; termination.all.learned_cap_reached falls by at least 55% against the fresh baseline chunk (316,337 on seed 1000, 323,598 on seed 1001) while termination.all.plan_complete stays within 3% of it (119,950 / 124,518); treated steps per run on the long grid arms in [0.58, 0.78] and on grid-short in [0.75, 0.95], read on chunk 1.
prediction.falsifier: Separation gate failed on chunk 1 (untreated depth>=8 or depth>=6 gap-over-cap share above 0.10): close without a rung read. Per-run depth>=8 treated over untreated below 0.95, or pooled depth>=10 per run below 0.85 over two chunks (the cut removes events); or cross-binary depth>=8 per explore-second below 1.05 with stops at or above the floor (the saved steps do not reach the wall clock, as the closed stall-abort read 0.948 runs per second); or probe_over_cap_completions above 5% of probe completions (the cap cuts live runs). The per-run guard interval is read pooled over two chunks: with a 0.75 share the stock quarter carries about 2,500 depth-8 events per chunk, so a 0.95 floor resolves at two chunks.
prediction.costClause: Cross-binary runs per explore-second at or above 1.10; per-step wall of the untreated quarter within 3% of the baseline (the acted compare at every handler entry must not cost measurable time).
prediction.judgeSeparationNote: research/observations/OBSERVATIONS.md records stall-abort-quantile-off-identity-path (closed): acted-bit quiescence with a p90 threshold from completed runs lost depth monotonically (d>=8 0.784) and slowed the session (runs/s 0.948) in a pre-learned-cap regime with purgatory delays on; it retired the family until an observable is shown to separate never-gains-depth from quietly-working. The chunk-1 separation gate above is that demonstration, built into the candidate rather than run as a census; the candidate is admitted on the regime change (learned cap engaged, purgatory off, cap-reached runs measured as client redirect loops with no state change) and not on the old question being open.

hypothesis.notes: Diagnosis, for the record and not for this candidate: the stalls are a liveness gap of the VR spec as written. A replica sends Recovery exactly once and never retries, and a primary that is restarted within a step or two of its crash (the Recover runnable is dispatched at priority ~1.0 in the next few steps) draws responses only from backups still in its own view, so the primary-of-latest-view response it needs is its own and never comes; NewEntry on a recovering node that believes itself primary answers with a redirect to itself, so ClientInterface loops. The paper leaves the retry unspecified (Ambiguous/implementation), it is a liveness not a safety matter, and bin/spur is protected, so the explorer can only stop paying for it. Not proposed: the placebo recovery-weight walk (recovery_weight_placebo.decisions 1.38B, flipped 0) and the quick-fire offer path (quick_fire_offers 1.16M, decisions 4,439, flipped 0) are dead but cost under 2% of wall, below the readable floor; the client hold's expiry-only release (908,006 expiry vs 139 dry) is by decision since the window was ablated as ornament at iteration 33 and the merged rule is the 64-step deferral.
hypothesis.redTeam: Strongest case against: the loop already tried this signal and retired it. OBSERVATIONS.md (stall-abort-quantile-off-identity-path, closed) used acted-bit quiescence with a threshold learned from completed runs and read a monotone-in-depth loss (d>=4 0.889 down to d>=8 0.784) with runs/s 0.948, and concluded that long no-act stretches are the normal texture of a run walking toward a deep interleaving because fault-injected deliveries mostly do not change state; the fresh baseline still reads receiver_restarted acted 0.14% and sender_restarted 18.6%. The candidate calibrates on completed probes, the population the log named as the wrong one, and does not cite the precedent. Its evidence that the tails are inert is one 60 s campaign on a loaded host (n 662 probe gaps), not reproducible here. The whole gain is throughput on the cross-binary rung where the settle-stop precedent under-read its band (1.065 vs [1.10, 1.30]); tail steps priced at 4 us mean the wall saving is well under the step saving, and the old stall-abort's bookkeeping made its session slower. Ending 75% of cap-reached runs early also changes the replay corpus's parents' tapes only if the cut precedes the signal, which it should not, and starves nothing the learners read, as argued; that part holds.
hypothesis.scoreReason: Mechanism-to-observable path is explicit and nearly every checkable claim reproduces on the merged tree: run_cap.rs constants (QUANTILE 0.99, HEADROOM 1.5, MIN_COMPLETED_SAMPLES 200, doubling checkpoints, over_cap counter, decay/reset), the node_state_token compare at scheduler.rs:1450 and :1455, RunOutcome variants and the deadlock exit in path.rs, the fresh baseline's termination split (50/31/19), steps_released_sum near steps_sum with a tiny tail_without_release, the 23-step/55% and sixth-of-steps/+6.5% precedents in the pool. What holds it at 6 rather than 7-9: the load-bearing premise (a quiet gap separates stuck from working) was refuted once in an earlier regime and the candidate's own evidence for it in this regime is a single unreproducible diagnostic. The rewrite adds a chunk-1 separation gate on the untreated quarter so the premise is read before the rung; with that it is falsifiable cheaply. Cost 0: no exec.rs, history.rs or linearizability-recording touch; a new termination outcome like the merged cap. Keeps bit 1<<10 (1024) as ranked first; PCT and the replay-arm candidate move.

reviewSummary: Seven candidates, none rejected, all verified against the merged tree (spur d051f69) and the fresh baseline cache afeccdf6e8f7. The stall cap ranks first at 6 (cost 0) after a load-bearing omission was found: OBSERVATIONS.md records the stall-abort family closed and retired on the same acted-bit progress signal with a monotone-in-depth loss and slower sessions; the regime has changed enough that the question is open, and a chunk-1 separation gate (untreated depth>=8 and depth>=6 runs' longest quiet gap against the standing cap, at most 5%) is written into its prediction so the premise is read before the rung. Its cross-binary floor 1.10 clears the layout floor and the 7-8% spread only at its low end. Replay-arm serving carries at 5 with stale fidelity references corrected to the merged baseline (0.478/0.453; the description's 0.39 remains false) and a power note; counter folding carries at 6-2 with every identity reproduced on the fresh baseline; the stall-release child at 4 stands alone only by carrying its parent, and its one-sided internal contrast floor is raised to 1.02; the headroom dose at 4 rides the stall cap's tail blind, with its band floor raised to 1.08 so it clears the spread, and must run in a separate session from the stall cap. PCT carries at 3 and the cover-edge reversal at 2, both unchanged. Bits: stall cap keeps 1<<10, stall release 1<<12, headroom 1<<16; PCT moves to 1<<11 / 1<<17; replay-arm moves to 1<<22 / 1<<23 (all verified unread in spur-core; decide.ts now derives its off-roster selftest bit, so 4096 is usable). Ties at net 4 are ordered counters, stall-release, headroom by independence of mechanism. Checkable claims found false: the replay candidate's 0.39 fidelity base and its GridArm::pick name; the stall cap's implicit claim that no prior stall mechanism exists in the record.

otherCandidates.scoreReason: Carried from iteration 75 at gain 5; nothing in the merge changes the miswiring it fixes, and choose() is verified to record util_stats draws so a side-effect-free peek is genuinely needed. Seed<C> carries cfg and config_index but not arms, as the candidate says. It is an enabling fix of a recorded defect, not a member of the retired replay-prefix ranking or arm-selector posterior families. Held at 5 rather than higher because the expected per-run effect sits at the resolution floor on a thin cell. Rewritten: stale fidelity references and the bit assignment; the description's 61%/38,161-of-98,033 figure remains false on every available baseline (0.45-0.52).
otherCandidates.redTeam: Strongest case against: the effect is small and thin. Iteration 28 read 1.080 on depth 8 at fidelity 1.0 stratified; lifting a quarter of prefix slots from 0.45-0.48 to about 0.7-0.8 buys 2-3 fidelity tenths, so the per-run lift on that quarter is 2-4%, at or below the harness's 2% resolution floor, on 4.5% of runs (about 550 depth-8 events per chunk): the frozen band's low end is unreadable before four chunks. The matched cell inherits the parents' arm mix by construction (a slot is served the parent that agrees with its own draw), which is a milder form of the balance fault that closed inherit-bits on cost. Exact matches among 64 ring parents over 72 arm sets may be rare for cells that are still exploring; the nearest-parent fallback then delivers partial fidelity and the mechanism degrades toward stock. The description still carries the 0.39 fidelity base the previous judge found false; on the merged tree the stock reference has moved again (0.45-0.48).

predictionRewrite.mechanism: Treatment bit replayArmMatched = 1<<12 on a quarter of prefix slots drawn by a salted phase of the run id; inverse bit replayArmMismatched = 1<<10 on another quarter; the stock half of prefix slots is the matched control (co-bits replaySlot and replayPrefix). Per-run depth>=8 ratio of the matched quarter to the stock prefix half, probe-free and matched on co-bits, in [1.03, 1.12] (base fidelity on the merged tree's fresh baseline (afeccdf6e8f7) is 0.478 (seed 1000) and 0.453 (seed 1001), so the lift available is about 0.25-0.30 fidelity units on the quarter); the mismatched quarter in [0.86, 0.99]. Tape interaction: the bits change which parent tape a slot receives and never how a run consumes or records one; parents are admitted only from fresh runs; the only shared coupling is ring consumption order. The child's would-be Choice depends on the parent's config cell, so the matched cell's arm mix may drift toward the parents' mix: expected balance fault on the arm co-bits, read through co-bit matching, and checked by the steps-per-child clause. Firing: replay.arm_match.exact >= 12,000 per chunk and replay.arm_match.children on the matched cell >= 20,000. JUDGE BIT ASSIGNMENT: bits 1<<10 and 1<<12 go to the higher-ranked stall-cap family; this candidate takes replayArmMatched = 1<<22 (4194304, retired staleFirstPair row) and replayArmMismatched = 1<<23 (8388608, retired crashPhaseOnLanding row), both unread in spur-core, renamed in VARIANT_BITS in the same commit.
predictionRewrite.independentObservable: Prefix fidelity per cell (replay.arm_match.faithful / children): matched cell >= 0.70 against the stock cell's 0.43-0.50 (merged baseline 55,044/115,217 = 0.478 and 53,024/117,005 = 0.453); mismatched cell <= 0.30. Exact-match children fidelity >= 0.95 (the bits-equal control read 0.987 at iteration 28). Steps per child within 2 percent across the three cells. Power note: the matched quarter is about 29k runs per chunk (4.5% of runs) carrying about 550 depth-8 events, so the [1.03, 1.12] interval cannot resolve at its low end before four chunks; the fidelity clauses are the chunk-1 read.
predictionRewrite.falsifier: Refuted if the matched-cell depth>=8 per-run interval lies entirely below 1.03, or if matched-cell fidelity is below 0.62 with the firing floor met, or if exact-match children read fidelity below 0.90 (the match is not pinning the prefix: shared learned state diverges, file that finding), or if mismatched-cell fidelity is not below the stock cell's. Matched-cell fidelity above 0.75 with depth>=8 flat is recorded as a finding against the corpus's cut, not against the fix.
predictionRewrite.costClause: Cross-binary throughput >= 0.98 of the paired baseline (serving costs at most 64 peeks per prefix slot); matched-cell steps per run <= 1.02x the stock cell.

otherCandidates.scoreReason: Carried from iteration 75 at gain 6, cost 2. Every checkable identity reproduces on the merged tree: 218 fetch_add sites on static AtomicU64s in util_stats.rs, the five per-step counters equal each other exactly, ranking_pass_skipped equals contested_decisions, and no_weighted_predicate equals steps_used_sum minus no_schedule_attempt. The prediction is byte-identical schedules with a counter-identity falsifier, so it is exactly reproducible seed for seed. Cost 2 stands: it rewrites the event-accounting layer that measurement validity rests on. Stale baseline figures updated.
otherCandidates.redTeam: Strongest case against: the hot spot is unprofiled. Relaxed fetch_add on x86 is a locked add; if the cache lines are not actually bouncing (each thread's run is long, and the hardware may keep lines in a shared-modified state cheaply), ten atomics cost 50-100 ns per step against a 6.5 us step (1.47B steps over 300 s x 32 threads), which is 1-2%, inside the 5% layout floor, and the candidate closes as unseparable. The 292 consecutive statics are false-shared across a few lines, which argues the other way, but nothing measured says so. The fold must also cover error and early-return paths in run_single_simulation or counts are lost, and the utilization dump is the instrument every other candidate's firing floor is read from, which is why it carries cost 2.

predictionRewrite.mechanism: No treatment bit: the contention removed is shared by every thread, so the candidate is graded on the cross-binary rung only. Per-run depth>=8 must read identically 1.00 (byte-identical schedules); the band is on depth>=8 events per explore-second over the rate stratum (grid arms, AOS excluded), expected in [1.05, 1.15], carried entirely by runs per second. Tape interaction: none. Firing: steer_reach.no_weighted_predicate >= 1e9 per chunk and equal to termination.all.steps_used_sum minus steer_reach.no_schedule_attempt (the merged tree's fresh baseline reads steer_reach.no_weighted_predicate 1,468,752,468 against steps_used_sum 1,468,752,503 with 35 no-schedule steps on seed 1000), which is the identity the fold must preserve.
predictionRewrite.independentObservable: On a deterministic-slice session every folded counter total equals the baseline binary's on the same seed and run count within 0.1 percent (steps, decisions, biased steps, deliveries, timer fires, crash-anchor offers); the campaign's per-arm run counts move only with the wall clock; grid plan_complete share and steps per run within 0.5 percent of baseline. Named baseline values to reproduce on the golden slice: the five per-step counters equal each other exactly, ranking_pass_skipped equals multiplier_authority.contested_decisions exactly. On the merged baseline the five per-step counters (steer_reach.no_weighted_predicate, steer_empty_slice.candidate_mask_skipped, steer_empty_slice.queue_audit_skipped, multiplier_authority.decisions, recovery_weight_placebo.decisions) all read 1,468,752,468 and ranking_pass_skipped equals contested_decisions at 594,420,962; these are the identities the fold reproduces.
predictionRewrite.falsifier: Refuted if cross-binary depth>=8 events per explore-second or runs per explore-second read below 1.05 of the paired baseline (inside the 5 percent layout floor: no separable gain, close), or if any folded counter total drifts from the baseline by more than 0.1 percent on the deterministic slice (counts lost, including runs that error before the fold), or if per-run depth>=8 reads outside [0.99, 1.01] or any shared run id differs in steps_used or end_reason (a schedule moved, which this change must not do).
predictionRewrite.costClause: Cross-binary throughput >= 1.05 of the paired baseline (this is the gain, not a cost); memory per run within 1 KB of baseline.
